sections.title: Monochromatic arm exponents for critical planar percolation
sections.abstract: The paper determines the critical planar percolation monochromatic three-arm exponent by an explicit positive-operator spectral threshold and gives spectral characterizations for all monochromatic n-arm exponents with n ≥ 4.
sections.claimed_result: The author reports that ξ₃ is the unique spectral threshold of an explicit integral-operator family and numerically evaluates it as 0.76928375…; the paper also characterizes ξₙ spectrally for n ≥ 4.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Critical planar site percolation on the triangular lattice, with three disjoint arms of one color across an annulus; the derivation uses CLE/LQG coupling and a boundary observable retaining past connections.
sections.unique_caveat: The three-arm value is characterized by an operator and numerical evaluation, not a simple closed form; the n ≥ 4 result is a spectral characterization rather than a list of evaluated constants.

sections.title: On the one-arm probability for the metric graph Gaussian free field in high dimensions
sections.abstract: For sign clusters of the Gaussian free field on cable systems, the authors establish power-law one-arm bounds from volume-growth and Green-function-decay exponents, including a logarithmic loss in the critical upper bound.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove θ(x,R) is bounded above and below by constants times R⁻ᵝ when 2α < 3ν; at 2α = 3ν, the lower bound remains cR⁻ᵝ and the upper bound is CR⁻ᵝ log(1+R). For ℤᵈ, the regimes correspond to d > 6 and d = 6.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A transient, locally finite weighted graph satisfying uniform ellipticity, volume growth V(B(x,R)) ≍ Rᵅ, and Green-function decay g(x,y) ≍ d(x,y)⁻ᵛ; β = α − ν.
sections.unique_caveat: The critical theorem does not give matching bounds up to constants; the paper notes that sharper asymptotics for ℤ⁶ are addressed in forthcoming work, not established by this paper.

sections.title: A near-quadratic lower bound for the Brown--Erdős--Sós (9,6)-problem
sections.abstract: For a 3-uniform hypergraph avoiding six edges on at most nine vertices, the authors prove a lower bound n² exp(−O((log n)²ᐟ³)), resolving the first unsolved case of a broader conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove f₃(n,9,6) ≥ n² exp(−O((log n)²ᐟ³)), where f₃(n,e+3,e) is the maximum number of edges in an n-vertex 3-uniform hypergraph with no e distinct edges spanning at most e+3 vertices.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: 3-uniform hypergraphs; the result treats the specific parameter pair (e+3,e) = (9,6) and asserts the bound asymptotically in n.
sections.unique_caveat: The result settles e = 6 only; the conjectured near-quadratic lower bound for every fixed e ≥ 3 remains broader than the case proved here.

sections.title: On the van der Corput property for cubes
sections.abstract: The authors prove a power-saving version of the van der Corput property for cubes and derive a power-saving upper bound for subsets of [N] with no nonzero cube differences.
sections.claimed_result: The authors obtain |A| ≪ε N^(59/60+ε) for A ⊆ {1,…,N} containing no nonzero difference that is a cube.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite subsets of the first N positive integers; the stated bound is for every ε > 0, with the implicit constant allowed to depend on ε.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract establishes this exponent but does not claim it is optimal or characterize extremal cube-difference-free sets.

sections.title: Transfer of Weisfeiler-Leman equivalence under graph operations
sections.abstract: The authors determine how much Weisfeiler-Leman equivalence is needed before selected graph operations preserve k-dimensional equivalence, exactly for line graphs and in several generalized line-graph regimes.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove τL(k) = 2k+1 for k ≥ 2 and τL(1) = 1; for (r,S)-line graphs they give τr,S(1) = r−1, exact values rk+r−1 for specified S when k ≥ r, and bounds in the remaining range.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Equivalence is that induced by k-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman graph-isomorphism tests; results concern line graphs and the stated family of clique-based (r,S)-line graph operations.
sections.unique_caveat: Exact values are not obtained for every generalized operation and parameter range; the abstract says the remaining range is bounded rather than fully determined.

sections.title: Stable soliton resolution for the corotational Skyrme model
sections.abstract: Under corotational symmetry, the author proves uniqueness of stationary Skyrmions in each topological degree, global well-posedness in a nonlinear energy space, and stable soliton resolution for finite-energy solutions.
sections.claimed_result: The author states that every finite-energy corotational solution scatters to the Skyrmion of the same topological degree.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The classical Skyrme model restricted to corotational symmetry; initial data have finite energy and are treated in a nonlinear energy space.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is symmetry-restricted and does not establish soliton resolution for unrestricted Skyrme dynamics.

sections.title: On the abc conjecture
sections.abstract: Using adelic intersection theory, the author claims an effective height bound for genus-two curves over number fields and derives a weak abc-type inequality.
sections.claimed_result: The author states that for a genus-two curve C over a number field K₀, points P over finite extensions F satisfy h(P) ≤ (12+ε) log|ΔF|/[F:ℚ] + β(ε). The introduction derives c ≤ A(ε) rad(abc)^(24+ε) for coprime positive integers a+b=c.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A smooth, projective, geometrically irreducible genus-two curve over a number field; the stated point-height inequality ranges over finite extensions and points rational over those extensions.
sections.unique_caveat: The derived exponent 24+ε is much weaker than the classical abc bound with exponent 1+ε; this preprint does not claim to prove the full abc conjecture. Its proof has not been independently assessed here.
